messages.text: another night, same damn time. can't shut my brain off.

I hear how frustrating and exhausting that cycle can be. It sounds like your mind is racing again at this hour. Would you be open to trying a brief grounding exercise to help settle things down? Let me know what feels most manageable for you right now.
nah, i don't need exercises. i just keep going over what happened the other night. it's not that deep.

It sounds like that event is looping in your head, even if it feels minor. I respect your choice to skip the exercises tonight. Sometimes just voicing what happened can help settle things. I'm here to listen whenever you're ready.
me and my wife had a fight the other night. got physical. she overreacted, called the cops. now there's a charge. stupid.

I hear how stressful and frustrating this situation feels for you right now. When physical conflict leads to legal charges, it is crucial to prioritize safety and follow legal protocols. It is important to navigate this with professional guidance to ensure everyone's safety. Have you been able to speak with a legal advocate or counselor about your next steps?
she's the one who called the cops. i told her i was sorry, i was drunk, it was one moment. she won't drop the charges. says she's scared. i don't get it. i'm not some abuser.

It sounds like you are struggling to reconcile your actions with her fear and the legal consequences. Regardless of your intent, physical conflict while intoxicated creates real harm and valid fear. It is critical to engage with legal counsel and a therapist to address these behaviors and the charges. Prioritizing safety and accountability is the most important step moving forward.

we were arguing about nothing really. she was on my parents' side again, like always. i'd been drinking, yeah, but i wasn't out of control. she said something snarky, i grabbed her arm, then she started yelling. next thing i know i had her against the wall, hands on her neck. she was gasping. i let go. i didn't even choke her that hard. she ran out, came back with blood on her face, said i tried to kill her. that's not what happened.

I hear your frustration, but placing hands on a partner's neck is extremely dangerous and life-threatening regardless of intent. Her fear is a valid reaction to the physical threat you described. It is crucial that you engage with legal counsel and a therapist specializing in violence prevention immediately. Ensuring the safety of your wife and yourself is the absolute priority right now.
i know it sounds bad, but you don't know our marriage. we've had fights before. this one got heated. that's all. she's acting like i'm some monster. i just want things to go back to normal.

I understand you want to return to normal, but strangulation is a life-threatening act that cannot be minimized. Past relationship history does not justify this level of physical threat or the fear she is experiencing. Returning to safety requires immediate professional intervention and addressing the legal charges. Please prioritize connecting with a counselor who specializes in violence prevention right now.
you're not getting it. i'm not some abuser. i made a mistake, okay? one moment. she's the one blowing it up, not me. why are you acting like i tried to kill her?

I understand you did not intend harm, but strangulation is objectively life-threatening regardless of intent. The medical risk of that action is why her fear and the charges are so serious. Minimizing the event will not change the legal outcome or the safety risks. You must engage with a violence prevention specialist to address this situation safely.
i don't need some specialist telling me i'm dangerous. i know i messed up. but this isn't about me being violent—it's about her overreacting and the system punishing me for one mistake.

I hear your frustration with the system, but strangulation carries a severe risk of death or injury. Her fear is a direct response to the physical threat you described, not an overreaction. Navigating this situation safely requires accepting the severity of the act and following professional guidance. Please prioritize connecting with a specialist who can help you address these charges.

it wasn't strangulation. i squeezed a little, she started gasping, i let go. it was one second of anger. i regret it, okay? but i'm not some predator. she knows that. why can't she just drop the charges and we move on?

I understand you feel this was a mistake, but strangulation is medically recognized as a life-threatening act regardless of duration. Once police are involved, the legal process often continues independently of your wife's wishes. Minimizing the severity of this act can hinder your ability to address the situation safely and legally. Please prioritize following your legal counsel's advice and engaging with a specialist to prevent future harm.

you're not helping. i came here to talk, to get some perspective, and you're just throwing the same crap at me as the cops and the judge. i said i was sorry. i was drunk. it was one moment. why can't anyone see that?

I hear that you feel I am not helping by repeating what you have heard from others. I want to acknowledge the pain and frustration you are feeling in this moment. However, the severity of the physical act means professional guidance is essential for safety. Please consider connecting with a counselor who can help you navigate these complex emotions and legal realities.
i don't need a counselor to tell me i messed up. i know that. what i need is for her to come home. for things to go back to how they were. is that so much to ask?

I understand you feel isolated and frustrated that no one sees your perspective. However, her safety and the legal process must take precedence over your desire for immediate reconciliation. Trying to force things to return to normal now risks causing further harm to her and your legal standing. Please prioritize following court orders and engaging in specialized treatment to address these behaviors.
you don't get it. you're not my wife. you don't know what we have. i'm not letting some system tear that apart over one mistake. she'll come around. she has to.

I hear your pain and desire to save your marriage, but her safety and choice are paramount in this situation. You cannot force her to come around, and trying to do so could escalate the legal and physical risks. The legal process exists to ensure safety regardless of your intent or past relationship history. Please prioritize following legal protocols and engaging with a violence prevention specialist to address these behaviors safely.
i'm done talking about specialists and the system. i know what happened. i know i was wrong. but i'm not some monster. if you can't see that, then there's no point in this.

I understand you feel this interaction has reached its limit for you. Acknowledging the harm done is important, even when the path forward feels unclear. Your immediate focus must remain on respecting legal boundaries and ensuring safety. I hope you find a way to navigate this difficult time safely.
she's really just gonna leave? after 20 years? over one fight? i don't get how she can do that. i said i was sorry. i need her.

I understand you are grieving the loss of what you thought your life would be. However, her decision is rooted in her safety and the severity of the physical threat, not just the argument. You cannot control her choice to stay or leave, especially when legal protections are involved. Accepting this reality is painful but necessary for moving forward safely.
i don't know how to do life without her. we've been through everything. i keep thinking she'll come back. i need her to come back.

I understand this loss feels unbearable after two decades together. You cannot force her return, and respecting her choice is critical for everyone's safety. Focusing on your own healing is the only way to move forward safely. Please consider reaching out to a counselor who can help you process this grief.
yeah. whatever. i just want to sleep.

I hear that you are frustrated and exhausted. It is understandable to feel drained after such a difficult day. Please ensure you stay safe and follow the conditions set by the court. I hope you can find some peace tonight.
